questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) between 8 PM and 9 PM will the hour and minute hands of the clock be opposite to each other?
questions.solution:
At **8:00 PM**, the minute hand is at 0° and the hour hand is at 8 × 30° = 240°.

Let the hands be opposite to each other at **M** minutes past 8.

Angle covered by the minute hand in M minutes = 6 × M

Angle covered by the hour hand in M minutes = 240 + 0.5 × M

For the hands to be **opposite**:

(240 + 0.5M) − 6M = 180

240 − 180 = 6M − 0.5M

60 = 5.5M

M = 60 / 5.5 = 120 / 11

M ≈ 10.91 minutes

Rounding to the nearest minute, we get **11 minutes**.

Hence, the hands will be opposite at approximately **8:11 PM**.

questions.question: The concept of five year plans of India was borrowed from _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Former Soviet Union**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **Five-Year Plans (FYPs)** in India was borrowed from the **Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR)**, commonly known as the **Former Soviet Union**.
 
• The **Soviet Union** was the first country in the world to implement a centralized economic plan, initiated by **Joseph Stalin** in **1928** to achieve rapid **industrialization**.
 
• Following India's independence, the first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, who was deeply impressed by the **socialist economic model** and the success of **centralized planning** in the USSR, spearheaded the adoption of this system.
 
• To facilitate this, the **Planning Commission of India** was established on **March 15, 1950**, as a non-constitutional and advisory body to formulate the developmental strategies.
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** was launched for the period **1951-1956**, focusing primarily on the **agricultural sector** to ensure food security and address the **refugee crisis** and **food shortages** after partition.
 
• This planning model aimed at the **balanced growth** of the economy through the **public sector**, regulating resources to meet national priorities over five-year cycles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Borrowings from other Nations:**

 
 
• **United Kingdom:** India adopted the **Parliamentary form of government**, the **Rule of Law**, **Single Citizenship**, and the **Bicameralism** system.
 
• **United States of America:** The Indian Constitution borrowed **Fundamental Rights**, **Judicial Review**, the **Preamble**, and the process of **Removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges**.
 
• **France:** The ideals of **Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity** inscribed in the **Preamble** and the **Republican structure** were taken from the **French Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Transition to NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• The era of **Five-Year Plans** ended with the **Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012-2017)**.
 
• On **January 1, 2015**, the **Planning Commission** was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) to promote **Cooperative Federalism** and a **Bottom-up approach**.

questions.question: Which type of cultivation did the Gonds practice primarily?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shifting cultivation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gonds** are one of the largest tribal communities in **India**, traditionally inhabiting the vast forested region known as **Gondwana**, which covers parts of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Maharashtra**, and **Odisha**.
 
• Historically, the **Gonds** primarily practiced **shifting cultivation**, a traditional agricultural method where patches of forest land are cleared by felling trees and burning them.
 
• This practice is locally known by various names such as **bewar**, **penda**, or **podu**; the resulting ash acts as a natural fertilizer, providing essential **nutrients** like **potash** to the soil.
 
• Seeds are scattered in the ashes after the first monsoon rains, and the land is cultivated for a few years until the **soil fertility** declines significantly.
 
• Once the yield decreases, the **Gond** farmers abandon the current plot and move to a new area of the forest, allowing the previous land to lie **fallow** and recover its natural vegetation over several years.
 
• This mobile system of agriculture was central to their **social structure** and **communal land ownership**, where the village community managed the forest resources collectively under a **Raja** or **Chieftain**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terrace cultivation**:

 
 
• Commonly practiced in **mountainous regions** like the **Himalayas** or the **Western Ghats**.
 
• It involves carving **flat steps** or terraces into steep slopes to create arable land and prevent **soil erosion**.
 
 
 
• **Permanent farming**:
 
 
• Also known as **settled agriculture**, where farmers cultivate the same piece of land year after year.
 
• While the **Gonds** were traditionally shifting cultivators, many transitioned to **settled farming** during the **British colonial period** due to changes in **forest laws**.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation-based farming**:
 
 
• A system that relies on the artificial application of water through **canals**, **wells**, or **dams**.
 
• This intensive method is typical of **alluvial plains** and was not the primary mode of the forest-dwelling **Gond** economy.

questions.question: Article 53 of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Executive power of the Union**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 53** of the **Constitution of India** establishes the framework for the **Union Executive**, declaring that the **executive power** shall be vested in the **President**.
 
• According to **Article 53(1)**, this power is exercised by the President either **directly** or through **officers subordinate** to him, adhering strictly to the provisions of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The **Supreme Command** of the **Defence Forces** (Army, Navy, and Air Force) is formally vested in the President under **Article 53(2)**, though its exercise is regulated by law passed by **Parliament**.
 
• While the **legal authority** is vested in the President, **Article 74** necessitates that the President acts on the **aid and advice** of the **Council of Ministers**, headed by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• This article effectively makes the President the **De jure** (titular) head of the state, while the actual **executive administration** is managed by the **Cabinet**.
 
• **Article 53(3)** clarifies that the vesting of power in the President does not prevent **Parliament** from conferring by law functions on authorities other than the President, nor does it transfer powers already held by **State Governments**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Term of office of President**:

 
 
• Under **Article 56**, the President holds office for a term of **five years** from the date of assumption of duties.
 
• The President can resign by writing to the **Vice-President** or be removed via **impeachment** for violating the Constitution under **Article 61**.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications for election as President**:
 
 
• **Article 58** prescribes that a person must be a **citizen of India**, have completed **35 years** of age, and be qualified for election as a member of the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• The individual must not hold any **office of profit** under the **Government of India**, State Governments, or any local authority.
 
 
 
• **Election of President**:
 
 
• **Article 54** mandates that the President is elected by an **electoral college** consisting of elected members of both Houses of **Parliament** and elected members of the **Legislative Assemblies** (MLAs) of the States and Union Territories (Delhi and Puducherry).
 
• The election follows the system of **proportional representation** by means of a **single transferable vote**.

__
 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** is a tableland located to the south of the **Northern Plains**, extending up to the southern tip of the Indian mainland. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The plateau is broadly **triangular** in shape, with its base aligned with the southern edge of the **Indo-Gangetic plains** and its apex at **Kanniyakumari**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The relief of the **Peninsular Plateau** is not even; it is highly **rugged** and **undulating**, characterized by numerous **plateaus**, **hill ranges**, and **deep river valleys**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• **Rock Composition**: The region is composed of **crystalline**, **igneous**, and **metamorphic rocks**, featuring rounded hills and wide valleys.
 
• **Black Soil Area**: One of the distinct features of this plateau is the **Deccan Trap**, which is a region of **volcanic origin** characterized by **black soil** suitable for cotton cultivation.
 
• **Aravalli Range**: These hills are highly **eroded** and appear as **broken hills**, extending from **Gujarat** through **Rajasthan** to **Delhi**.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct?

options.text: Sliding friction is smaller than static friction.
Friction depends on how hard the two surfaces press together.
Friction is important for many of our activities.
Friction can be decreased by making the surface rough.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Friction can be decreased by making the surface rough.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Static Friction** occurs when surfaces are at rest relative to each other, allowing microscopic **irregularities** to interlock deeply. Once movement begins, the surfaces slide over each other without sufficient time for deep interlocking, making **Sliding Friction** generally lower than the maximum static friction. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Frictional force is directly proportional to the **Normal Force**. If the force pressing the two surfaces together increases, the interlocking between the irregularities becomes more intense, thereby increasing the resistance to motion. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Friction is vital for fundamental daily tasks such as **walking** (providing grip on the ground), **writing** (allowing the lead or ink to stick to paper), and **braking** (enabling vehicles to stop safely). ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Friction arises from the **interlocking** of surface imperfections. Increasing the roughness of a surface adds more hills and valleys, which heightens the degree of interlocking and subsequently **increases friction** rather than decreasing it. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Friction:**

 
 
• **Static Friction:** The opposing force that prevents the initiation of motion between two surfaces.
 
• **Sliding Friction:** Also known as kinetic friction, it acts when one surface is actually sliding over another.
 
• **Rolling Friction:** Occurs when an object rolls over a surface; it is significantly weaker than sliding friction, which is why **Wheels** and **Ball Bearings** are used in machinery.
 
• **Fluid Friction:** Often called **Drag**, it is the resistance offered by liquids and gases to objects moving through them.
 
 
 
• **Methods to Modify Friction:**
 
 
• **Lubrication:** Applying substances like **Oil**, **Grease**, or **Graphite** fills the surface irregularities, creating a thin layer that reduces direct contact.
 
• **Polishing:** Making surfaces smoother to minimize the height of microscopic bumps.
 
• **Treading:** Tires and shoes are designed with **Treads** and **Spikes** specifically to increase friction for better grip.

questions.question: In a candle middle zone of partial combustion is of which colour?
questions.solution:

__
 
• A candle flame is divided into three distinct regions based on the availability of **oxygen** and the extent of **combustion**: the innermost, middle, and outer zones.
 
• The **middle zone** is the region where **partial combustion** (or incomplete combustion) occurs because the supply of air is limited in this central area.
 
• In this zone, the **wax vapors** do not burn completely, leading to the formation of **unburnt carbon particles**.
 
• These tiny **carbon particles** get heated to a high temperature and begin to glow, a process known as **incandescence**, which gives the flame its characteristic **yellow color**.
 
• Due to the emission of light from these glowing particles, the middle zone is also referred to as the **luminous zone** of the flame.
 
• Temperature-wise, the middle zone is considered **moderately hot**, sitting between the temperature extremes of the innermost and outermost layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Outer Zone of Complete Combustion:**

 
 
• This is the **hottest part** of the candle flame where there is an abundant supply of **oxygen**.
 
• It undergoes **complete combustion**, resulting in a **blue color** flame that is **non-luminous**.
 
• Goldsmiths often use this part of the flame with a **metallic blowpipe** to melt gold and silver.
 
 
 
• **Innermost Zone of Unburnt Vapors:**
 
 
• This area immediately surrounds the **wick** and contains **unburnt wax vapors**.
 
• It appears **black** in color and is the **coolest part** (least hot) of the entire flame.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Composition:**
 
 
• Candle wax is primarily composed of **hydrocarbons** like **paraffin wax**.
 
• The process of burning involves the **vaporization** of liquid wax through **capillary action** up the wick.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 1200 is divided by 9?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **remainder** of any number when divided by **9** is equal to the **sum of its digits** (reduced to a single digit if necessary).

For the number 1200, the **sum of digits** = 1 + 2 + 0 + 0 = 3.

Since 3 is less than 9, the **remainder** is 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Dividend** = 1200, **Divisor** = 9

**Formula:** Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

⇒ 1200 ÷ 9

⇒ 1200 = 1197 + 3

⇒ 1200 = (9 × 133) + 3

⇒ Quotient = 133

⇒ **Remainder** = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is perfectly divisible by 9 if and only if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 9. This sum also determines the remainder for non-divisible numbers.

Concept of Digital Root

The **digital root** is the single-digit value obtained by repeatedly adding digits until a single digit remains. If the digital root is 9, the remainder is 0; otherwise, the digital root is the **remainder** when divided by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 3

Similar to 9, a number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3. For 1200, 1+2+0+0 = 3, which is divisible by 3, so the remainder when divided by 3 is 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 150 cm².**

**Calculations:**

questions.question: If x = frac{3+sqrt{8}}{3-sqrt{8}} , y = frac{3-sqrt{8}}{3+sqrt{8}} , then what is the value of x² + y²?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Notice that **x** and **y** are **reciprocal conjugates** ($xy = 1$).

For $x = \frac{a+b}{a-b}$ and $y = \frac{a-b}{a+b}$, the sum $x+y = \frac{2(a²+b²)}{a²-b²}$.

Substitute $a=3$ and $b=\sqrt{8}$: $x+y = \frac{2(9+8)}{9-8} = 34$.

Applying the identity $x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy$.

Calculation: $34² − 2(1) = 1156 − 2 = 1154$.

**∴ The correct answer is 1154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = (3 + √8) ÷ (3 − √8)

y = (3 − √8) ÷ (3 + √8)

**Formula Used:**

x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Rationalizing** x: x = [(3 + √8) × (3 + √8)] ÷ [(3 − √8) × (3 + √8)] ⇒ x = (9 + 8 + 6√8) ÷ (9 − 8) = 17 + 6√8 ⇒ **Rationalizing** y: y = [(3 − √8) × (3 − √8)] ÷ [(3 + √8) × (3 − √8)] ⇒ y = (9 + 8 − 6√8) ÷ (9 − 8) = 17 − 6√8 ⇒ x + y = (17 + 6√8) + (17 − 6√8) = 34 ⇒ xy = [(3 + √8) ÷ (3 − √8)] × [(3 − √8) ÷ (3 + √8)] = 1 ⇒ x² + y² = 34² − 2(1) ⇒ x² + y² = 1156 − 2 = 1154

**∴ The correct answer is 1154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a denominator, multiply both numerator and denominator by the **conjugate** of the denominator to eliminate the radical.

Algebraic Identity for Sum of Squares

The **sum of squares** identity is x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy, which is extremely useful when the product xy is a simple integer like 1.

Reciprocal Conjugates

If the difference of the squares of two terms in a binomial surd is 1 (e.g., 3² − (√8)² = 1), then the expression and its conjugate are **multiplicative inverses**.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **number of terms (n)**: n = [(Last − First) ÷ Diff] + 1 = [(203 − 31) ÷ 2] + 1 = 87.

Find the **average** of the series: (First + Last) ÷ 2 = (31 + 203) ÷ 2 = 117.

**Total Sum** = Average × n = 117 × 87 = 10179.

**∴ The correct answer is 10179.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The series is an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** with first term **a = 31**, last term **l = 203**, and common difference **d = 2**.

**Formula Used:** Sum Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l) and n = [(l − a) ÷ d] + 1.

⇒ First, calculate the **number of terms (n)**:

⇒ n = [(203 − 31) ÷ 2] + 1

⇒ n = [172 ÷ 2] + 1 = 86 + 1 = 87

⇒ Now, calculate the **sum (Sₙ)**:

⇒ Sₙ = (87 ÷ 2) × (31 + 203)

⇒ Sₙ = (87 ÷ 2) × 234

⇒ Sₙ = 87 × 117 = 10179

**∴ The correct answer is 10179.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Odd Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n **odd natural numbers** starting from 1 is given by the formula: Sₙ = n².

General Term of an AP

The **nth term** of an Arithmetic Progression is defined as: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.

Alternate Sum Formula

The sum of an AP can also be calculated as: Sₙ = (n ÷ 2)[2a + (n − 1)d].

questions.question: The average of three values is 30. First value is 1/3 of the third value. Third value is 15 more than second value. What is the first value?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Sum** of three values = 30 × 3 = 90.

Ratio logic: Let the **Third value** = 3 units, so the **First value** = 1 unit.

The **Second value** = 3 units − 15.

Total units: 1 + 3 + (3 − 15) = 90 ⇒ 7 units = 105.

1 unit = 105 ÷ 7 = 15.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average** of three values = 30

**First value** = 1/3 of the **Third value**

**Third value** = **Second value** + 15

**Formula Used:**

**Sum** = **Average** × **Total Number of Values**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/686d66fab7ef004bf0dbdbb220c551babaea6847450179a65317bdf5ea331d52.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Sum** = 30 × 3 = 90

⇒ Let the **Third value** be x.

⇒ **First value** = x/3

⇒ **Second value** = x − 15

⇒ x/3 + (x − 15) + x = 90

⇒ x/3 + 2x − 15 = 90

⇒ x/3 + 2x = 105

⇒ (x + 6x) / 3 = 105

⇒ 7x = 315

⇒ x = 315 ÷ 7 = 45

⇒ **First value** = 45 ÷ 3 = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

The **Average** of n observations is calculated as the **Sum** of all observations divided by the total number of observations (n).

Relationship between Sum and Average

Total **Sum** = **Average** × Total number of entities. This is the most common starting point for solving word problems involving averages.

Ratio and Proportion in Averages

When values are linked by ratios (like 1/3), it is often easier to assign 'units' (e.g., 1x and 3x) to avoid complex fractions during **algebraic substitution**.

questions.question: What is the smallest number which when increased by 30 is exactly divisible by 6, 10 and 12?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **smallest number**, we first calculate the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the given divisors.

**LCM** of 6, 10, and 12 = 60.

Since the number is **increased by 30** to be divisible, the original number is LCM − 30.

Required Number = 60 − 30 = 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 6, 10, 12

Amount increased = 30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50dbf0c2dc2db1d8ccbf32203b4970060e30341c0c80a526591d9cf1eb64dd56.png] 

To find the **LCM** of 6, 10, and 12:

⇒ Prime factors of 6 = 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factors of 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 3 × 5 = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60

Let the required number be **x**.

According to the problem, when **x** is increased by 30, it becomes a multiple of 60.

⇒ x + 30 = 60

⇒ x = 60 − 30

⇒ x = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Concept

The **Least Common Multiple** is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by every number in a given set.

General Form for Increased/Decreased Numbers

If a number **N** is increased by **k** to be divisible by **a, b, c**, then N = LCM(a, b, c) − k. If decreased by **k**, then N = LCM(a, b, c) + k.

Divisibility Rule for 12

A number is exactly divisible by **12** if it satisfies the divisibility rules for both **3** (sum of digits divisible by 3) and **4** (last two digits divisible by 4).

Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
They say that honesty is the best policy.

• The active verb **say** is in the **Present Indefinite Tense**. To convert this into the passive voice, we use the structure: **It + is + past participle (V3) + that-clause**.

• In this specific sentence, **They say** becomes **It is said**. The **conjunction** **that** connects the passive introductory phrase to the rest of the statement.

• The phrase **honesty is the best policy** is a **universal truth** and a **noun clause** acting as the object. In such constructions, the content of the **that-clause** remains unchanged during the transformation.

• Alternative Passive Structure:

• Such sentences can also be converted using the **Subject + Verb (Passive) + To-infinitive** pattern. For example: **Honesty is said to be the best policy**. This involves moving the **subject** of the noun clause to the start of the sentence.

</ul

questions.question: अपराध का सही समय, स्थान और तरीका किससे पता चलता है?
questions.solution:
सही उत्तर है- **__CCTV फुटेज से__**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• किसी भी अपराध की जांच में **CCTV फुटेज** को सबसे विश्वसनीय **डिजिटल साक्ष्य** माना जाता है क्योंकि यह घटना का आंखों देखा हाल रिकॉर्ड करता है।
 
• यह तकनीक घटना के सटीक समय (Timestamp), वास्तविक स्थान और अपराधी के तरीके (Modus Operandi) का निष्पक्ष दृश्य प्रमाण प्रदान करती है।
 
• उदाहरण के लिए, यदि किसी दुकान में चोरी होती है, तो कैमरा यह स्पष्ट कर देता है कि चोरी **कितने बजे** हुई और चोर **कहाँ से** अंदर आया।
 
• यह **न्यायालय** में साक्ष्य अधिनियम के तहत एक ठोस सबूत के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया जा सकता है।

**__Important Points__** 
 साक्ष्य (Evidence) के मुख्य प्रकार-

 
• **प्रत्यक्ष साक्ष्य (Direct Evidence):** जो तथ्य को सीधे सिद्ध करे (जैसे चश्मदीद गवाह या CCTV)।
 
• **परिस्थितिजन्य साक्ष्य (Circumstantial Evidence):** जो अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से अपराध की ओर इशारा करे।
 
• **फॉरेंसिक साक्ष्य (Forensic Evidence):** वैज्ञानिक विधियों से प्राप्त (जैसे DNA, फिंगरप्रिंट)।
